name: Programming
summary: Learn to think in code by breaking problems down, writing programs and debugging until they work.

name: Python
summary: The friendliest first language, used for scripts, data, automation, AI and nearly everything else.

name: Web Development
summary: Build websites and web apps with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, then add servers, databases and deployment.

name: App Development
summary: Design and ship your own mobile app, from the first screen to the app store.

name: Data Science
summary: Clean, explore and model real datasets to answer questions with statistics and code.

name: Machine Learning
summary: Train models that learn from data, from linear regression to neural networks, and understand why they work.

name: Building with AI
summary: Build apps, agents and automations on top of large language models, from prompt design to tool use.

name: Competitive Programming
summary: Solve algorithm puzzles against the clock in online contests, where speed and cleverness both count.

name: Open Source Contributing
summary: Fix bugs and add features to projects used by millions, learning git, code review and collaboration.

name: Hackathons
summary: Build something from scratch with a team in a weekend, then demo it to the room.

name: Linux
summary: Get comfortable in the terminal with shells, permissions, packages and scripting, and make the system yours.

name: Home Lab & Self-Hosting
summary: Run your own servers at home for media, backups, password vaults and anything else you want to own.

name: Cybersecurity
summary: Learn how systems are attacked and defended through networks, web apps and practice in hands-on labs.
safety: Only test systems you own or have written permission to test. Unauthorised access is a crime almost everywhere.

name: Capture the Flag
summary: Solve hacking puzzles in crypto, web, forensics and binary exploitation to capture flags in team contests.
safety: Keep your attacks to CTF platforms and systems you're explicitly authorised to test.

name: Reverse Engineering
summary: Take software and hardware apart to see how it really works, with disassemblers, debuggers and patience.
safety: Respect software licences and anti-circumvention laws. Practise on crackmes, your own code or devices you own.

name: Spreadsheet Wizardry
summary: Go beyond SUM with lookups, pivot tables, array formulas and dashboards that run themselves.

name: Touch Typing
summary: Type without looking at 80 or more words per minute with correct finger placement and lots of drilling.

name: Quantum Computing
summary: Learn qubits, superposition and entanglement, then run real circuits on cloud quantum hardware.

gear: Free quantum SDK and cloud access

name: Bots & Automation
summary: Write scripts and bots that do your boring tasks: chat bots, scrapers, alerts and scheduled jobs.

name: Shader Programming
summary: Write GPU code that paints every pixel at once, such as raymarched worlds, water and glowing effects.

name: Electronics
summary: Understand voltage, current and components, and build working circuits on a breadboard.

name: Soldering
summary: Make clean, reliable joints for through-hole parts, then surface-mount parts, wires and repairs.
safety: Use fume extraction, wash your hands after handling leaded solder and always return the iron to its stand.

name: Arduino & Microcontrollers
summary: Program tiny computers to read sensors and drive lights, motors and screens.

name: Raspberry Pi Projects
summary: Turn a credit-card-sized computer into a retro console, media centre, weather station or robot brain.

name: PCB Design
summary: Design your own circuit boards, from schematic to layout to a batch of manufactured boards.

name: Robotics
summary: Build robots that sense and move, combining mechanics, electronics and code, then enter competitions.

name: Home Automation
summary: Make your home smart on your own terms with sensors, routines and a local hub that doesn't need the cloud.
safety: Leave mains wiring to a qualified electrician unless you are trained and allowed to do it yourself.

name: Wearable Tech
summary: Sew LEDs, sensors and microcontrollers into clothes and costumes that light up and react.

name: 3D Printing
summary: Print parts, gadgets and miniatures, and learn slicing, tuning and designing for the printer.

name: Laser Cutting
summary: Cut and engrave wood, acrylic and leather with precision for signs, boxes, puzzles and gifts.
safety: Never leave a running laser unattended, extract the fumes and never cut PVC or vinyl, which release toxic chlorine gas.

name: CNC Machining
summary: Carve wood, plastic and aluminium with a computer-controlled router, from CAD to toolpaths to finished part.
safety: Wear eye and hearing protection, clamp work securely and keep your hands well clear of a spinning bit.

name: Amateur Radio
summary: Talk to the world over the airwaves, bounce signals off the ionosphere and help in emergencies.
safety: Transmitting needs an amateur radio licence. Pass the exam before you key up.

name: Software-Defined Radio
summary: Explore the radio spectrum with a cheap USB dongle: aircraft, weather satellites, pagers and more.
safety: Receiving is legal in most places, but transmitting needs a licence, and some countries restrict decoding or sharing private communications.

name: Retro Computing
summary: Restore, program and play vintage computers, from the Commodore 64 to classic Macs.

name: PC Building
summary: Pick compatible parts, build a computer from scratch, manage the cables and tune it for performance.

name: Mechanical Keyboards
summary: Build custom keyboards by choosing switches and keycaps, lubing, modding and tuning the sound.

name: Electronics Repair
summary: Diagnose and fix broken gadgets, consoles and audio gear instead of throwing them away.
safety: Unplug before opening anything. Capacitors can hold a lethal charge, so leave microwaves, CRTs and mains power supplies to experts.

name: Circuit Bending
summary: Rewire battery-powered sound toys into glitchy, unpredictable noise instruments.
safety: Only bend battery-powered devices. Never open anything that plugs into the mains.

name: DIY Synthesisers
summary: Build synths and Eurorack modules from kits, then design your own oscillators and filters.

name: Guitar Pedal Building
summary: Build fuzz, overdrive and delay pedals from kits, then mod them and design your own tone.

name: FPV Drones
summary: Fly acrobatic drones through goggles at 100 km/h: freestyle, racing and cinematic dives.
safety: Train in a simulator first. FPV flying is regulated in most countries, so learn the registration, licence and spotter rules, and fly away from people.
